domain.x-typeDescription:
The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

named-condition.description:
Individual named condition (Traffic Class) configuration entry.
Each named condition represents a specific traffic classification rule
that can be applied to network policies. The condition defines criteria
for matching network traffic based on various protocol headers and
application characteristics.

Named conditions provide reusability and consistency across multiple
policies, allowing network administrators to define traffic classes
once and reference them in various policy contexts such as network,
access control, and QoS.

association.description:
Association context for the named condition, defining the scope and application
domain where this traffic classification rule will be active. The association
type determines how the named condition integrates with different policy
network contexts within the system.

Association types typically include interface-specific or
role-based contexts, allowing for control over where traffic classification
rules are applied.

condition-rule.description:
Ordered list of traffic classification rules that collectively define the
named condition (Traffic Class). Each rule specifies matching criteria for
network traffic using various protocol headers and application characteristics.

All rules within this list must conform to the same classification type
as specified in the parent named condition's rules-type field.

count.description: Enable packet counting for traffic matching this rule.

description.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for this rule entry.

ignore.description:
When set to true, this rule is ignored during traffic
classification processing and no further action will be taken except
for log and count.

log.description:
Enable logging for traffic matching this rule when used in access control contexts.
This option is available only for network ACL rule types (Ethernet, IP, IPv6).
When enabled, matching traffic events are recorded in the system logs, providing
audit trails for security monitoring and troubleshooting.

position.description:
Sequential position number for this rule within the named condition's rule list.
Position determines the order of rule evaluation, with lower numbers processed
first. This ordering is critical for traffic classification logic where multiple
rules might match the same traffic flow. Position values must be unique within
the named condition and should allow.

description.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for the Named Condition (Traffic Class).

name.description:
Unique identifier for the named condition, which becomes the Traffic Class name
on the device. This name must be unique within the system and follows standard
naming conventions for network device objects. The Traffic Class name is used
by policies to reference this traffic classification rule.

reverse-named-condition.description:
Boolean flag to enable reverse functionality for role-based policies.
When enabled, this creates bidirectional traffic classification for role-based
access control, allowing policies to automatically apply matching rules in
both directions of communication flows.

rules-type.description:
Classification type for the named condition, determining which protocol layers
and fields are available for traffic matching.

Available types include:
- IP-based conditions: Match on network layer protocols and addressing
- Ethernet-based conditions: Match on data link layer MAC and VLAN information
- Application-based conditions: Match on identified applications and services

All rules within a single named condition must use the same classification type.

net-service.description:
List of network service definitions. Each net-service defines
a named protocol/port combination that can be referenced in
policy rules to match specific types of network traffic. The
key 'name' uniquely identifies the net-service.

alg-config.description:
Application Layer Gateway (ALG) configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). This container is only available when
alg-service is set to ICMP, DNS, FTP, MSRPC, or SUNRPC. Each
ALG type exposes its own sub-container with protocol-specific
configuration options.

alg-service.description:
Specifies the Application Layer Gateway (ALG) service type
for this net-service. ALG enables deep packet inspection
for application-specific protocols, allowing the firewall
to handle dynamic port negotiation and NAT traversal. The
selected ALG must be compatible with the configured protocol
(TCP, UDP, or other). See the must constraint for valid
protocol/ALG combinations.

x-enumDescriptions.DHCP:
Enables ALG for DHCP traffic allowing dynamic relay and
inspection of DHCP messages. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.DNS:
Enables ALG for DNS traffic allowing inspection and optional
filtering of DNS queries and responses. Requires UDP protocol.
Additional DNS ALG options can be configured via the alg-config
container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.FACETIME:
Enables ALG for Apple FaceTime video calling traffic.
Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.FTP:
Enables ALG for FTP traffic allowing inspection and NAT
traversal of FTP control and data connections. Requires TCP
protocol. Additional FTP ALG options can be configured via
the alg-config container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.H323:
Enables ALG for H.323 video conferencing and VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.ICMP:
Enables ALG for ICMP traffic allowing inspection by type
and code. Additional ICMP ALG options can be configured via
the alg-config container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.JABBER:
Enables ALG for Cisco Jabber unified communications traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.MSRPC:
Enables ALG for Microsoft RPC (Remote Procedure Call) traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol on port 135. Additional MSRPC
ALG options can be configured via the alg-config container.
x-enumDescriptions.NOE:
Enables ALG for Alcatel NOE (New Office Environment) VoIP
traffic. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.RTSP:
Enables ALG for RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) media
streaming traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SCCP:
Enables ALG for SCCP (Skinny Client Control Protocol) used
by Cisco IP phones. Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SIP:
Enables ALG for SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SIPS:
Enables ALG for SIPS (SIP over TLS) encrypted VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SUNRPC:
Enables ALG for SUN RPC (Remote Procedure Call) traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol on port 111. Additional SUNRPC
ALG options can be configured via the alg-config container.
x-enumDescriptions.SVP:
Enables ALG for SVP (SpectraLink Voice Priority) wireless
VoIP traffic. Requires a protocol other than TCP or UDP.
x-enumDescriptions.TFTP:
Enables ALG for TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol)
traffic. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.VOCERA:
Enables ALG for Vocera badge communication traffic.
Requires UDP protocol.

Application Layer Gateway (ALG) service types. Each ALG type
enables deep packet inspection for a specific application protocol,
allowing the firewall to understand and correctly handle protocol-specific
behavior such as dynamic port negotiation and NAT traversal.

description.description:
An optional human-readable description for this net-service.
Can be used to document the purpose or intended use.
Maximum length is 128 characters.

http-proxy.description:
When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTP
proxy port for web traffic interception. Only applicable
when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

https-proxy.description:
When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTPS
proxy port for secure web traffic interception. Only
applicable when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

name.description:
Unique name of the net-service. This is a required key field.
Maximum length is 63 characters.

port-range.description:
Port range specification for this net-service. If operator
is COMPARISON_RANGE, both min and max values define the range.
If operator is COMPARISON_EQ, only the min value is used as
the exact port match. Cannot be used together with the ports
leaf-list.

max.description:
Upper bound of port range. Only applicable when operator
is COMPARISON_RANGE. Must be greater than min. Protocol
must be TCP or UDP.
max.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

min.description:
Port value or lower bound of port range. When operator
is COMPARISON_EQ, this is the exact port to match. When
operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, this is the lower bound.
Protocol must be TCP or UDP.
min.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

operator.description:
Comparison operator for port matching. When set to
COMPARISON_EQ, matches a single port (min). When set
to COMPARISON_RANGE, matches all ports between min
and max inclusive. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

x-enumDescriptions.COMPARISON_RANGE: Minimum and maximum values of range.

is ICMP.

policy.description:
A firewall policy identified by a unique name. Each policy
contains an ordered set of rules that match traffic and
apply actions. ACL-type rules (RULE_ACL_IP, RULE_ACL_IPV6,
RULE_ACL_MAC) are only permitted in POLICY_NETWORK_ACL
policies.

association.description:
Specifies how this policy is associated with clients or
interfaces. Defaults to ASSOCIATION_ROLE (role-based
policy assignment).

description.description:
A user-defined description or comment for this policy.
Maximum 256 characters.

dsf-enable.description:
Enable distributed services firewall (DSF) for this policy.
When enabled, the policy type must be POLICY_TYPE_SECURITY.
Applicable to AOS-CX switches only. Defaults to false.

name.description:
Unique name of the policy. This is a required key field.
Maximum 145 characters. On AOS-CX, space (' ') and
question mark ('?') characters are not supported in
policy names.

type.description:
Type of policy. Determines the rule structure and actions
available. If dsf-enable is true, the type must be
POLICY_TYPE_SECURITY.

x-enumDescriptions.POLICY_NETWORK_ACL: Network Access Control List policy type.

policy.security-policy.policy-rule.description:
Ordered list of policy rules. Each rule defines a match
condition and action pair. Rules are evaluated in ascending
order by position (low to high). The key 'position' uniquely
identifies each rule within the policy.

description.description:
A user-defined description or comment for this policy rule.
Maximum length is 256 characters.

devices-applicable.description:
Read-only field indicating whether the rule is supported by
all or a subset of target devices. Values are 'full' (all
devices support this rule) or 'partial' (only some devices
support it).

position.description:
Sequence position that determines the order in which rules
are evaluated. This is a required key field. Lower values
are evaluated first. The position must be unique for each
rule within the policy.

policy.security-policy.policy-rule.condi.description:
List of TCP control flags to match (e.g., SYN, ACK, FIN, RST). Only applicable for TCP traffic.
Use this to match specific TCP connection states or control packets. Multiple flags can be specified.

items.description:
List of TCP control flags to match (e.g., SYN, ACK, FIN, RST). Only applicable for TCP traffic.
Use this to match specific TCP connection states or control packets. Multiple flags can be specified.

x-enumDescriptions.TCP_ECE:
TCP ECN-Echo flag.  If the SYN flag is set, indicates that
the TCP peer is ECN-capable, otherwise indicates that a
packet with Congestion Experienced flag in the IP header
is set

items.x-typeDescription: TCP flags to match

policy.security-policy.policy-rule.actio.description:

to. Up to 3 sessions can be appended. For PVOS switches only.

security-policy.policy-rule.condition.so.description:
List of user role names for source address matching. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_ROLE.
Matches traffic originating from users assigned to any of the specified roles. Each role name
can be up to 256 characters. For switch and gateway devices only.

items.description:

Matches traffic destined to users or resources assigned to any of the specified roles. Each role
name can be up to 256 characters. For switch and gateway devices only.

policy-group.policy-group-list.description:
An ordered list of firewall policies with their evaluation priorities.
Policies are evaluated in ascending order by position (lower values first).
Each policy name must be unique, and each position must be unique within the group.

description.description:
A user-defined description explaining the purpose or context of this policy's
placement in the evaluation sequence. Maximum length is 256 characters.

name.description:
Unique identifier for the firewall policy. This name must reference an existing
policy configured in the system. Maximum length is 256 characters.

position.description:
The evaluation priority of this policy in the global policy sequence. Policies are
evaluated in ascending order (lower numbers are evaluated first). This value must be
unique across all policies in the group. Valid range: 1 to 2000.

role.app-aaa-contract.app.description:
List of application-based bandwidth contracts keyed by application name
and traffic direction. Each entry maps a specific DPI application
(e.g. facebook, youtube, zoom) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for
either upstream or downstream traffic.

appname-direction.description: Key combination of application name and direction separated by '~'.

role.app-category-aaa-contract.app-categ.description:
List of application category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by
category name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a DPI application
category (e.g. STREAMING, GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) to a named AAA
bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.

category-name-direction.description: Key combination of application category name and direction separated by '~'.

role.web-category-aaa-contract.web-categ.description:
List of WebCC category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by WebCC category
name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC content category to
a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.
There can be at most one contract per category per direction.

webcategory-name-direction.description: Key combination of WebCC category name and direction separated by '~'.

role.web-reputation-aaa-contract.web-rep.description:
List of WebCC reputation-based bandwidth contracts keyed by reputation
risk level and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC reputation
level (TRUSTWORTHY, LOW_RISK, MODERATE_RISK, SUSPICIOUS, or HIGH_RISK)
to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream
traffic. There can be at most one contract per risk level per direction.

webrepname-direction.description: Key combination of WebCC reputation name and direction separated by '~'.

role.exclude-app-contract.exclude-app.description:

Each entry specifies an application name that will bypass any configured
bandwidth contract rate limits.

role.exclude-app-cat-contract.exclude-ap.description:
List of DPI application categories excluded from bandwidth contract
enforcement. Each entry specifies a category name (e.g. STREAMING,
GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) whose traffic will bypass any configured
bandwidth contract rate limits.

role.aaa-bw-contract.bw-contract.description:

direction. Each entry assigns a named AAA bandwidth contract to either
upstream or downstream traffic, with an optional
association scope of per-user or per-apgroup.

x-enumDescriptions.PER_APGROUP: Assign bandwidth contract per-apgroup (default is per-role).
x-enumDescriptions.PER_USER: Assign bandwidth contract per-user (default is per-role).

auto-cluster.description: With this knob enabled, gateways will be added to the auto-cluster/removed from the auto-cluster automatically by the System. This knob should be set to false while creating the manual cluster profiles.

id.description: This is an optional parameter which specifies the starting VRRP ID for cluster members. If this is not configured, system automatically configures VRRP groups starting with default VRRP ID of 220. This is only applicable while configuring VRRP for COA [Change of Authorization]. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for coa-vrrp id configuration.

passphrase.description: VRRP Passphrase. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for passphrase configuration.
passphrase.x-typeDescription:
A custom derived type for special use cases. This type takes a plaintext password and uses
Vault's 3rd party API to encrypt the password. The intended use case is to encrypt and store
customer credentials which will be used later to login to 3rd party services.

vlan.description: VRRP VLAN corresponding to the VIP. Used for COA operations.
vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

heartbeat-threshold.description: Gateway will wait for heartbeat threshold time (ms) before declaring a peer cluster node as dead.

ipv4-gateways.description:
Upto 12 gateways can be configured in a profile. Based on the combination of Gateway platforms, system will restrict Gateway addition to the profile.
Ex: Presence of 70xx model gateway in the profile will reduce the Gateway count to 4.

ipv6-enable.description: Enable or disable the ipv6 mode in cluster profiles. ipv6-enable knob can not be toggled once the cluster profile is created.

name.description: Gateway Cluster Profile name. Manual cluster profile name should not start with auto_ prefix and it should not contain space.

one-to-one-redundancy.description:
Enable/disable one-to-one-redundancy mode for the cluster profile.
With this knob enabled, only 2 gateways are allowed in the cluster profile.
Leader is active and non-leader is standby.

uplink-tracking.description:
Enable/disable uplink tracking for the cluster profile.
With this knob enabled, Cluster leader will be selected based on number of active uplinks.
Applicable only when one-to-one-redundancy knob is enabled.

split-policy.description:
Configures the split-policy for stack splits. It determines the behavior
of the fragments resulting from a stack split. This option is available
only for 2930M and 3810 stacks.

x-enumDescriptions.ALL_FRAGMENTS_UP:
Split policy as all fragments up. This is typically not recommended since the
fragments could share the IPs and may result in conflicting decision making.
x-enumDescriptions.ONE_FRAGMENT_UP:
Split policy as one fragment up. This is the default option. Only the fragment detected
to be active forwards the traffic. For active fragment detection, the management(OOBM)
port of all stack members should be connected to a peer L2 switch or hub.

lowercase characters.

shutdown-on-split.description:
Configures non-vsx interface to go down along with VSX interfaces during split.
This also configures the interface-vlan, whose vlan tag is not configured
on any of the MCLAGs, to go down on VSX split. In case of interface-vlans,
this command is recommended to be configured on those interface-vlans which
would establish L3 adjacency with other devices that are not
part of VSX MCLAGs but part of ISL and that would require immediate reconvergence
on VSX split.For example, VxLAN tunnels formed through VSX switches whose overlay routes
are advertised through these interface-vlans can be configured with this command.

Configures non-vsx interface to go down along with VSX interfaces during split.
This also configures the interface-vlan, whose vlan tag is not configured
on any of the MCLAGs, to go down on VSX split. In case of interface-vlans,

are advertised through these interface-vlans can be configured with this command.

profiles.description:
List of App Bandwidth Contract profiles. Each profile is identified by a
unique name and groups up to four types of directional bandwidth contracts:
DPI application (app), DPI application category (app-category), WebCC
reputation score (web-reputation), and WebCC category (web-category).
The combined total number of entries across all four contract lists within
a single profile must not exceed 32.

app.description:
List of bandwidth contracts keyed by DPI application name and traffic direction.
Each entry maps a specific application (e.g. facebook, youtube, zoom) to a
bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic. The application
name must be a valid DPI application type and the direction must be specified.
Bandwidth limits are configured via the bwc-units and bit-rate leaves.

app-name-direction.description: Key combination of DPI Application and direction separated by '~'.

app-category.description:
List of bandwidth contracts keyed by DPI application category and traffic direction.
Each entry maps a broad application category (e.g. STREAMING, GAMING,
SOCIAL-NETWORKING) to a bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream
traffic. This allows bandwidth policies to be applied at the category level
rather than per individual application. Bandwidth limits are configured via
the bwc-units and bit-rate leaves.

app-category-name-direction.description: Key combination of DPI Application Category and direction separated by '~'.

web-category.description:
List of bandwidth contracts keyed by WebCC category and traffic direction.
WebCC classifies web destinations into categories (e.g. BUSINESS-ECONOMY,
GAMES, EDUCATIONAL-INSTITUTIONS, SOCIAL-NETWORKING). Each entry maps one
WebCC category to a bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream
traffic, enabling bandwidth policies based on the type of web content being
accessed. There can be at most one contract per category per direction.

web-category-name-direction.description: Key combination of WebCC category and direction separated by '~'.

web-reputation.description:
List of bandwidth contracts keyed by WebCC reputation score range and traffic
direction. WebCC assigns a reputation score to each URL upon classification and
groups scores into the following risk levels: TRUSTWORTHY (81-100),
LOW_RISK (61-80), MODERATE_RISK (41-60), SUSPICIOUS (21-40), and
HIGH_RISK (1-20). Each entry maps one risk level to a bandwidth contract for
either upstream or downstream traffic, allowing differentiated bandwidth
treatment based on the trustworthiness of web destinations. There can be at
most one contract per risk level per direction.

web-rep-score-direction.description: Key combination of WebCC reputation score and direction separated by '~'.

dpi-enable.description:
Enable App Recognition features. This field enables Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) for AP, Gateway and CX Switches.
It also implicitly enables Web Content Classification (WebCC) for AP and Gateway only.
This is enabled by default for Microbranch & Campus APs, Mobility and Branch Gateways.
DPI uses Qosmos for classifying traffic into application & application category types.

webcc-cache-miss-drop.description:
WebCC caches classification data of a URL when it encounters it for the first time.
Enable this feature to drop session packets until a cache entry is found for the URL, i.e. until a WebCC
category or reputation score classification is available in the internal WebCC cache.
This feature is applicable to Gateway only. It is disabled by default.

webcc-enable.description:
Enable Web Content Classification (WebCC) feature for AP and Gateway.
This is enabled by default for Microbranch & Campus APs, Mobility and Branch Gateways.
It is mandatory to enable DPI to use WebCC.  WebCC feature uses the Brightcloud® URL database of categorie and
reputation risk scores to classify web traffic. An IP name server must be configured for this feature to work.

redirect-url.description:
Configure URL to redirect session to when users access a URL that matches a WebCC deny rule.
The URL must be prefixed with http:// or https:// . Permitted length is 5-250 characters.
Applicable to Gateway only.
redirect-url.x-typeDescription:
An ASCII-encoded Uniform Resource Locator (URL) as defined
in RFC 3986, section 1.1.3

url-visibility.description: Enable the URL visibility feature. Applicable to AP only.

webcc-connectiontype-ipv6.description:
Enable to force WebCC to use IPv6 for communicating with vendor service.
This configuration is disabled by default.
Disabling it makes WebCC fall back to dual-stack mode with IPv4 preferred.
This feature is applicable to Gateways only.

Air Pass approvals for Central NAC.

Air Pass approval defines site based approval requests for MNOs with the approval status.

approval-status.x-typeDescription: Approval status of the MNO request.

request-ts.description: Timestamp for when the approval request was generated.
request-ts.x-typeDescription:
A date and time, expressed in the format described in RFC3339.
That is to say:

YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ+-hh:mm

where YYYY is the year, MM is the month expressed as a two-digit
month (zero padding if required), DD is the day of the month,
expressed as a two digit value. T is the literal character 'T',
HH is the hour of the day expressed as a two digit number, using
the 24-hour clock, MM is the minute of the hour expressed as a
two digit number. Z is the literal character 'Z', followed by a
timezone offset expressed in hours (hh) and minutes (mm), both
expressed as two digit numbers. The time offset is specified as
a positive or negative offset to UTC using the '+' or '-'
character preceding the offset.

Optionally, fractional seconds can be expressed after the minute
of the hour as a decimal number of unspecified precision
reflecting fractions of a second.

response-ts.description: Timestamp for when the approval response was received.
response-ts.x-typeDescription:
A date and time, expressed in the format described in RFC3339.
That is to say:

YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ+-hh:mm

where YYYY is the year, MM is the month expressed as a two-digit
month (zero padding if required), DD is the day of the month,
expressed as a two digit value. T is the literal character 'T',
HH is the hour of the day expressed as a two digit number, using
the 24-hour clock, MM is the minute of the hour expressed as a
two digit number. Z is the literal character 'Z', followed by a
timezone offset expressed in hours (hh) and minutes (mm), both
expressed as two digit numbers. The time offset is specified as
a positive or negative offset to UTC using the '+' or '-'
character preceding the offset.

Optionally, fractional seconds can be expressed after the minute
of the hour as a decimal number of unspecified precision
reflecting fractions of a second.

A port profile defines parameters on the port such as VLAN settings, authentication methods, link speed, PoE settings, and more.

At least one port profile must be specified.

A port profile defines parameters on the port such as VLAN settings, authentication methods, link speed, PoE settings, and more.

For a CAPTIVE_PORTAL authentication profile, only wired interfaces with one of these port profiles will be configured with the captive portal.

At least one port profile must be specified.

At most 100 port profiles may be specified.

profile.captive-portal.sponsor-domains.description:
Allowed domain names for sponsor email addresses.

The maximum number of sponsor-domains allowed is 50.

When a user is registering an account that requires sponsor approval (see require-sponsor-approval), they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.

Anyone who has an email address in one of these domains is a valid sponsor.

The sponsor-domains list can only be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

See also the sponsor-emails field for configuring specific email addresses as valid sponsors.

Both the sponsor-domains and sponsor-emails lists define valid sponsors.

custom-message.description:
A custom message can be used with Central NAC portal profiles and visitor
management facilities to provide customized email and SMS messages for
Central NAC visitors.

description.description: A description, or note, for the custom message.

message-id.description: Unique identifier for the custom message (must be a UUID).

message-purpose.description:
The purpose of the custom message (e.g. PASSWORD_NOTICE, REGISTRATION, etc.).

The purpose defines where and how a custom message can be used, as well as
which replacement tokens must be included in the message.

The message types supported for each purpose are:

- PASSWORD_NOTICE: EMAIL, SMS
- REGISTRATION: EMAIL, SMS
- SPONSOR_APPROVAL: EMAIL only
- VERIFICATION_CODE: SMS only
- VERIFICATION_LINK: EMAIL only

The replacement tokens that must, or may, be included in the message content
for each purpose are:

- PASSWORD_NOTICE: may include: [account:username], [account:password]
- REGISTRATION: may include: [account:username], [account:password]
- SPONSOR_APPROVAL: must include: [account:sponsor-approval-url], may include: [account:username]
- VERIFICATION_CODE: must include: [account:verification-code]
- VERIFICATION_LINK: must include: [account:verification-url], may include: [account:username]

x-enumDescriptions.PASSWORD_NOTICE:
Specifies that the custom message can be used to notify the user about account
creation and password reset.

A password notice may contain the [account:username] and [account:password]
replacement tokens.
x-enumDescriptions.REGISTRATION:
Specifies that the custom message can be used to notify the user about
registration of their account.

A registration message may contain the [account:username] and
[account:password] replacement tokens.
x-enumDescriptions.SPONSOR_APPROVAL:
Specifies that the custom message can be used to notify the sponsor of a
registration request that requires their approval.

A sponsor approval message must contain the [account:sponsor-approval-url]
replacement token.

A sponsor approval message may contain the [account:username] replacement
token.

This purpose is only applicable to EMAIL messages.
x-enumDescriptions.VERIFICATION_CODE:
Specifies that the custom message can be used to send a verification code to
the user when registering an account.

A verification code message must contain the [account:verification-code]
replacement token.

This purpose is only applicable to SMS messages, as email messages use the
VERIFICATION_LINK purpose instead.
x-enumDescriptions.VERIFICATION_LINK:
Specifies that the custom message can be used to send a verification link to
the user when registering an account.

A verification link message must contain the [account:verification-url]
replacement token.

A verification link message may contain the [account:username] replacement
token.

This purpose is only applicable to EMAIL messages, as SMS messages use the
VERIFICATION_CODE purpose instead.

registration-email-message.description:
An optional custom email message to send on registration.

The message type of the referenced custom message must be EMAIL.

The message purpose of the referenced custom message must be REGISTRATION.

If not set, the default custom message of type EMAIL and purpose REGISTRATION
will be used. If no default custom message is defined, the system default
registration email message will be used.

registration-sms-message.description:
An optional custom SMS message to send on registration.

The message type of the referenced custom message must be SMS.

The message purpose of the referenced custom message must be REGISTRATION.

If not set, the default custom message of type SMS and purpose REGISTRATION
will be used. If no default custom message is defined, the system default
registration SMS message will be used.

require-accept-terms.description: Require the user to accept the terms and conditions of login page

sponsor-approval-email-message.description:
An optional custom email message to send when requesting sponsor approval.

The message type of the referenced custom message must be EMAIL.

The message purpose of the referenced custom message must be SPONSOR_APPROVAL.

If not set, the default custom message of type EMAIL and purpose
SPONSOR_APPROVAL will be used. If no default custom message is defined, the
system default sponsor approval email message will be used.

terms-location.x-typeDescription: Where the terms and conditions should be displayed

verification-code-sms-message.description:
An optional custom SMS message to send for verification.

The message type of the referenced custom message must be SMS.

The message purpose of the referenced custom message must be VERIFICATION_CODE.

If not set, the default custom message of type SMS and purpose VERIFICATION_CODE
will be used. If no default custom message is defined, the system default
verification code SMS message will be used.

verification-link-email-message.description:
An optional custom email message to send for verification.

The message type of the referenced custom message must be EMAIL.

The message purpose of the referenced custom message must be VERIFICATION_LINK.

If not set, the default custom message of type EMAIL and purpose
VERIFICATION_LINK will be used. If no default custom message is defined, the
system default verification link email message will be used.

background-color.description: The CSS color to apply to the background of the page
background-color.x-typeDescription:
A numerical CSS Color (Module Level 3).

Supported formats include:

#rgb             3 hex digit format

#rrggbb          6 hex digit format

rgb(r,g,b)       RGB functional notation with either 3 integers, or
                3 percentages

rgba(r,g,b,a)    RGBA functional notation with RGB values as per
                rgb(), and a 4th alpha-value

hsl(h,s,l):      HSL functional notation with H (hue) as either an
                integer (0 to 360) or a percentage, and
                S (saturation) and L (lightness) as percentages

hsla(h,s,l,a):   HSL functional notation with HSL values as per
                hsl(), and a 4th alpha-value

NOTE: alpha-values are only supported as floating point values,
        which should be in the range 0.0 (fully transparent) to 1.0
        (fully opaque).

profile.description:
Defines a single AP System profile containing all system-level configurations for one or more
Access Points. Each entity is identified by name. Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete
an instance.

advanced-zone.description:
Enable or disable the advanced zone feature that can configure up to 32 SSIDs.
Since the mapping method of the WLAN index and BSSID index are different,
when you change the advanced zone configuration, the BSSID is removed and created again.
When advanced zone is enabled:
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 A zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 16 SSIDs.
 However, if the extended SSID is disabled,
 a zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 14 SSIDs wherein the first two virtual APs are reserved for mesh.

advertise-ap-health-ie.description:
Control AP to enable/disable 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature. This feature is enabled by default.
'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature controls AP to broadcast the AP health IE through the wireless SSIDs.
The AP health IE contains many flags that can reflect current AP status like uplink status,
Central connectivity status. Once AP lost Central connection, this AP health IE can be broadcast through
wireless beacons so that our Aruba APs nearby can hear this beacon and send the AP health IE to Central.
This will allow the user or engineer to understand the status of the issue AP and take measures to rescue it.

advertise-location.description:
Enable advertising location info in beacon frame.
Disable by default.

allow-new-aps.description: Allows the new access points to join the AP cluster. This API is AOS8 specific.

allow-new-aps-alias.description: Alias for allow new aps. This API is AOS8 specific

allowed-ap.description:
Specifies the MAC address of an AP permitted to join the cluster. Available on firmware versions up to 10.0.0.
This setting is specific to AOS8 platforms.

items.description:
Specifies the MAC address of an AP permitted to join the cluster. Available on firmware versions up to 10.0.0.
This setting is specific to AOS8 platforms.

application-monitoring.description:
Enables application monitoring on the AP.
Available on firmware versions 8.6.0 to 8.11.99 only.

cluster-security.description:
Cluster Security DTLS configuration for IAP.
Enabling cluster-security dtls will form Datagram TLS connection between Conductor and Member APs.

allow-low-assurance-devices.description: Allow non-TPM (Trusted-Platform-Module) devices to connect over DTLS

allow-non-dtls-members.description: Do not allow non-DTLS enabled APs to connect

conductor.description: Provisions the Instant AP as a conductor Instant AP. This API is AOS8 specific.

conductor-alias.description: Alias for conductor. This API is AOS8 specific.

content-filtering.description:
Content filtering configuration at system level.
This option control access to websites and applications based on their content, adding more security.

country-code.description: Defines the country of operation of an AP.

country-code-alias.description: Alias for virtual controller country code.

dhcp-option82-xml.description:
Configure DHCP Option 82 XML file. The AP inserts circuit and remote ID information
into DHCP requests from clients.

x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_1_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 1. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: AP Name, AP MAC Address, Extended AP MAC Address,
Remote ID: User's MAC Address.
x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_2_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 2. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: AP MAC Address, Extended AP MAC Address, SSID Tunnel,
Remote ID: User's MAC Address.
x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_3_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 3. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: User's MAC Address,
Remote ID: AP Name, Extended AP MAC Address.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: No DHCP Option 82 XML file will be used.

dhcp-option82-xml.x-typeDescription: Enumeration of allowed DHCP Option 82 XML file names.

dhcp-option82-xml-vlan-list.description:
VLAN or VLAN range for which DHCP Option 82 XML applies. Allowed values: a single VLAN (1-4094)
or a range (e.g., 10-100). This leaf can only be configured when dhcp-option82-xml is set to a valid XML file.
dhcp-option82-xml-vlan-list.x-typeDescription:
VLANs or only single-tagged VLANs or both. A range is
specified as x-y where x and y are valid VLAN IDs
(1 <= vlan-id <= 4094). The range is assumed to be inclusive,
such that any VLAN-ID matching x <= VLAN-ID <= y falls within
the range.

disable-factory-reset.description:
Disable the factory reset function on the AP. Prevent the manual hard reset to factory default by pressing
down reset button for 5 seconds.

drt-upgrade-disable.description: Disable the automatic download and installation of DRT updates on the AP managed by Aruba Central.

dynamic-cpu-mgmt.description: Enable/Disable Dynamic CPU management to manage resources across different functions performed by an AP.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO:
Configure the AP to automatically enable or disable CPU management feature during run-time.
When configured, the AP determines the need for enabling or disabling CPU management, based
on the real-time load calculations taking into account all different functions that the CPU
needs to perform. The auto option is the default and recommended setting.
x-enumDescriptions.DISABLE: Disable the CPU management feature, typically for small networks. This setting protects the user experience.
x-enumDescriptions.ENABLE:
Enable the CPU management feature. When configured, the client and network management functions
are protected. This setting helps in large networks with a high client density.

enet-vlan.description: Configures VLAN for the upstream switch to which the AP is connected.

extended-ssid.description:
This command allows you to configure additional WLAN SSIDs.
Extended SSID is enabled in the factory default settings of APs.

fips-enable.description:
Enable/Disable FIPS mode for AP. When enabled, AP operates in compliance with FIPS
and utilizes approved cryptographic algorithms and modules for enhanced security.
Note that toggling this knob will lead to a reboot of the AP.

firsthop-security.description:
Controls first hop security features on the AP. When enabled, security features are active.
Available on firmware versions 10.7.1 and later.
By default these security features are enabled on the AP.

ip-mode.description:
Selects the IP mode for packet processing.
IPV4_ONLY processes only IPv4 packets; IPV4_PREFER prioritizes IPv4 over IPv6.

x-enumDescriptions.IPV4_ONLY: Enables system processing of IPv4 packets.
x-enumDescriptions.IPV6_ONLY: Enables system processing of IPv6 packets. Not supported on Microbranch APs.

ip-mode.x-typeDescription: IP mode to process IPv6 or IPv4 packets.

itm.description:
Enable Intelligent Thermal Management(ITM) on the AP. When enabled, certain operations of the
AP will be throttled down to reduce its internal temperature. The limitations of AP operations
is defined by the priority assigned for reduction steps configured in Intelligent Power Monitoring(IPM)
API. IPM must be enabled for ITM to function.

lacp.description:
Enable/Disable/Remove the static LACP(Link Aggregation Control Protocol) configuration.
When an AP boots up, it forms the LACP according to the static configuration.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: This parameter enables the dynamic LACP configuration. The AP will work on LACP mode only if the peer switch works on.
x-enumDescriptions.DISABLE:
This parameter disables the static LACP configuration. The AP will not work on LACP mode even it detects any LACP PDUs
from the peer switch.
x-enumDescriptions.ENABLE:
This parameter enables the static LACP configuration. The AP will work on LACP mode irrespective of whether or not the
peer switch works on the LACP mode.

led.description: Enable LED display on an AP.

led-override.description: Override the LED action for LED operation mode normal.

led-tap.description: Enable LED tap detection on APs. Currently, this feature is only supported on AP605H.

mas-integration.description: Enables mobility Access Switch integration on an AP.

module.description:
List of logging module configurations for specifying severity levels by type, process,
and subcategory. Capacity constraints apply on a per-context basis.

severity.description:
Minimum severity for logging.
Range: EMERGENCY, ALERT, CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, NOTICE, INFO, DEBUG.
severity.x-typeDescription: Logging level upto which, the messages are logged.

type-process-subcategory.description: Key combination of type, process and subcategory separated by '~'.

mtu.description:
Configure the MTU size for tunnel and br0 interfaces, and uplink interface such as 3G or 4G.
The configured MTU size is applied when the uplink changes.

out-of-service-hold-on-time.description:
Configure a hold on time in seconds, after which out-of-service operation is triggered.
For example, if the Internet is unreachable, the effect of this out-of-service state impacts the SSID
availability after the configured hold on time.

poe-power-optimization-enable.description:
Enable optimization minimizes the POE draw of the AP and may disable some parts of the AP. The USB
and Ethernet port (eth1) are shut down on the AP when this option is enabled. The AP will operate in
the full power mode when this option is disabled. It is disabled by default on the AP.

recovery-ssid-backoff-time.description:
Configures the backoff time in minutes before bringing up the recovery SSID.
When the AP disconnects from Central, the recovery SSID will be brought up after this backoff period.
The recovery SSID type can be configured in the wlan-ssid profile and provides access to the AP's troubleshooting interface.

swarm-mode.description: Provision an Instant AP in the standalone, single AP, or cluster mode. This API is AOS8 specific.

mode.description:
Provisions the Instant AP in the standalone, single AP, or cluster mode.
Range: CLUSTER, STANDALONE, SINGLEAP.
Note: SINGLEAP value is unsupported on firmware versions up to 8.7.9.

x-enumDescriptions.CLUSTER: Instant AP in the cluster mode, it can form a cluster with other Virtual Controller Instant APs in the same VLAN.
x-enumDescriptions.SINGLEAP:
Instant AP in the single AP mode, it does not send or receive management frames such as mobility packets, roaming packets,
hierarchy beacons through the uplink port.
x-enumDescriptions.STANDALONE: Instant AP in the standalone mode, it cannot join a cluster of Instant APs even if there are other Instant APs in the same VLAN.

mode.x-typeDescription: Provisions the Instant AP in the standalone, single AP, or cluster mode.

system-vlan.description:
System-VLAN for Microbranch AP. This is L3-Enabled VLAN, mapped to IPMS-system-IP-Pool.
IPMS service will use this VLAN-id, allocate a /32 IP from the corresponding system-ip-pool,
and populate the inner-ip field in ap-system profile for each Microbranch AP.
system-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

tx-blanking.description:
Controls TX blanking for Ultra Tri-Band (UTB) channel scanning. When enabled, resolves 5GHz/6GHz co-existence interference.
Available only on models: AP-735A, AP-755A.

utb-filter-block.description:
Controls which radio band the UTB uplink traffic limitation is applied to.
Supported values: UTB_6GHZ (default, applies limitation to 6 GHz band) or UTB_5GHZ (applies limitation to 5 GHz band).

profile.description:
A Gateway System profile instance encapsulates all device-level operational settings for a gateway.
Each profile is uniquely identified by the profile name.
Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete a Gateway System profile.

aaa-timers.description: Configures timeout intervals for AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) operations including server failure detection, user idle sessions, logon attempts, and RADIUS accounting updates.

dead-time.description:
Dead time interval in minutes for a down authentication server.
Value of 0 disables dead time.

idle-timeout.description: Inactivity timeout for authenticated users in minutes. If no traffic is detected from a user for this duration, the session is terminated and re-authentication is required. This parameter is mutually exclusive with idle-timeout-seconds.

idle-timeout-seconds.description:
User idle timeout in seconds.
Valid range is 30-15300 seconds in multiples of 30 seconds.
This field can be configured only if idle-timeout is not configured.

logon-lifetime.description: Maximum session duration for captive portal or web-authenticated users in minutes. After this time expires, the user must re-authenticate via the captive portal even if the session is active. Value of 0 disables the maximum lifetime, allowing sessions to persist until idle timeout or explicit logout.

stats-timeout.description: Interval for sending RADIUS Interim-Update accounting messages in minutes. These updates provide periodic usage statistics (bytes transferred, session duration) to the RADIUS server for active user sessions. Mutually exclusive with stats-timeout-seconds.

stats-timeout-seconds.description: User Interim stats timeout value in seconds. This field can be configured only if stats-timeout is not configured.

auth-trace-loglevel.description:
Enable authentication tracing with specified syslog level threshold.
All authentication-related syslog messages at or above this severity will be traced.

x-enumDescriptions.ALERT: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_ALERT
x-enumDescriptions.CRITICAL: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_CRIT
x-enumDescriptions.DEBUG: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_DEBUG
x-enumDescriptions.EMERGENCY: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_EMERG
x-enumDescriptions.ERROR: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_ERR
x-enumDescriptions.INFO: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_INFO
x-enumDescriptions.NOTICE: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_NOTICE
x-enumDescriptions.WARN: Trace all logs equal or higher than LOG_WARN

auth-trace-loglevel.x-typeDescription: Syslog severity level threshold for authentication tracing. All authentication-related syslog messages at or above this severity will be traced.

contact.description: Device contact information, often an email.

cpdns-disable.description: Disables the gateway's automatic DNS redirection for captive portal detection. When enabled, the gateway will not intercept DNS queries from unauthenticated clients to force captive portal discovery. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-ip.

cpdns-ip.description: Specifies a custom IP address returned in DNS responses to unauthenticated clients, forcing redirection to the captive portal. This overrides the default behavior of returning the gateway's own IP address. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-disable. Corresponds to the `ip cp-redirect-address` CLI command.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

datapath-energy-efficiency.description:
Minimizes idle CPU spinning. It is applicable only on x86 based platforms.
Not supported on Gateway models: 7005, 7008, 7010, 7024, 7030, 7205, 7210, 7220, 7240, 7240XM, 7280.

dns-query-interval.description: Interval for re-resolving DNS hostnames configured in RADIUS and authentication server profiles. This ensures the gateway maintains current IP addresses for servers specified by FQDN rather than static IP.

dos-profile.description: Reference to DOS profile from gw-system profile. This config option will not pushed to the device.

fips.description: Enable the Fips knob on the Aruba Gateway.

firewall.description: Defines device-wide firewall behaviors that apply to all traffic regardless of user role or VLAN. These settings control inter-user traffic isolation, jumbo frame support, and VoIP QoS trust models.

deny-inter-user-bridging.description:
Prevents the forwarding of Layer2 traffic between wired or wireless users.
You can configure user role policies that prevent Layer3 traffic between users or networks but this does not block Layer2 traffic.
This option can be used to prevent traffic, such as Appletalk or IPX from being forwarded.
If enabled, traffic (all nonIP traffic) to untrusted port or tunnel is also blocked.

deny-inter-user-bridging-allowed-address.description: Configure IPv4/IPv6 addresses to be exempted when deny-inter-user-bridging is enabled. Total IPv4 and IPv6 allowed addresses can't exceed 256

ip-address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address that needs to be allowed

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted decimal notation.
Excludes invalid/reserved addresses:
- 0.0.0.0 (unspecified address)
- 127.0.0.0/8 (loopback addresses)
- 224.0.0.0/4 (multicast addresses, 224-239.x.x.x)
- 255.255.255.255 (limited broadcast address)

An IPv6 address represented in standard notation (full, compressed, or mixed formats).
Does not include zone identifiers (e.g., %interface).
Excludes invalid/reserved addresses:
- :: (unspecified address, all zeros)
- ::1 (loopback address)
- ff00::/8 (multicast addresses, ffxx:...)

mac-address.description: mac-address that needs to be allowed

deny-inter-user-traffic.description:
Denies downstream traffic between users in a wireless network (untrusted users) by disallowing layer2 and layer3 traffic.
This parameter does not depend on the deny-inter-userbridging parameter being enabled or disabled.

drop-ipv4-options.description: When enabled, all IPv4 packets with options are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

enable-stateful-icmp.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

enforce-tcp-handshake.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

enforce-tcp-sequence.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

jumbo.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with default MTU value 9216

jumbo-mtu.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with custom MTU value. Valid range is 1789-9216

voip-qos-trusted.description: Prioritizes the RTP traffic based on the DSCP value set by the end user device

drop-ipv6-options.description: When enabled, all IPv6 packets with options are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

enable-stateful-icmp.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

enforce-tcp-handshake.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

enforce-tcp-sequence.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

first-hop-security-profile.description: Reference to First hop security profile from gw-system profile. This config option will not pushed to the device.

gps.description: Enable the GPS function on the Aruba modem. Available only on 9004-LTE (Gateway with integrated cellular modem)

ipv4-configuration.description:
System IPv4 configurations, allows you to set either
the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface
address. If the system IPv4 is not configured, then
the first configured VLAN interface address is selected
by the device.

device-interface-type.description:
Specifies the interface type used for the system controller IPv4 address.
When set to VLAN, the device-vlan or device-vlan-alias parameter must also be specified to identify which VLAN interface to use. Corresponds to the `controller-ip` CLI command.

x-enumDescriptions.LOOPBACK: Uses the loopback interface IP address as the system identifier. Recommended for stable addressing as loopback interfaces remain up regardless of physical link state.
x-enumDescriptions.VLAN: Uses a VLAN interface IP address as the system identifier. The system will use the primary IP address configured on the specified VLAN.

device-interface-type.x-typeDescription: Defines the interface type used for system-level IP addressing (controller-ip). This determines which IP address the gateway uses to identify itself to managed devices, RADIUS servers, and routing protocols.

device-vlan.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IPv4 address configured on this VLAN will be used as the controller-ip. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN.
device-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

device-vlan-alias.description:
Alias for device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with device VLAN identifier field.

ipv6-certification-mode.description: Enables IPv6 certification test mode for compliance validation. This mode adjusts protocol timers and behaviors to match IPv6 conformance test requirements (e.g., IPv6 Ready Logo testing). Should only be enabled in test environments.

ipv6-configuration.description:
System IPv6 configurations, allows you to set either
the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface
address. If the system IPv6 is not configured, then
the first configured VLAN interface address is selected
by the device.

device-address.description:
Specific IPv6 address to use as the controller-ipv6 identifier. This address must be pre-configured on the VLAN interface specified in device-vlan.
Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN. This parameter is restricted to device-level scope and cannot be applied at site or global levels.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.
device-address.x-typeDescription:
An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

device-interface-type.description: Device interface type to indicate either loopback or VLAN interface.

x-enumDescriptions.LOOPBACK: Uses the loopback interface IP address as the system identifier. Recommended for stable addressing as loopback interfaces remain up regardless of physical link state.
x-enumDescriptions.VLAN: Uses a VLAN interface IP address as the system identifier. The system will use the primary IP address configured on the specified VLAN.

device-interface-type.x-typeDescription: Defines the interface type used for system-level IP addressing (controller-ip). This determines which IP address the gateway uses to identify itself to managed devices, RADIUS servers, and routing protocols.

device-vlan.description:
Device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.
device-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

ipv6-device-vlan-alias.description:
Alias for IPv6 device VLAN and address configuration, only applicable when device interface type is VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with direct device-vlan and device-address.

ipv6-enable.description: Master enable for IPv6 protocol support on the gateway. When disabled, the device will drop all IPv6 packets and will not participate in IPv6 routing or forwarding.

ipv6-proxy-ra.description: Configures the gateway to act as an IPv6 router advertisement proxy, forwarding RA messages between network segments. This allows IPv6 clients on downstream VLANs to receive router advertisements from upstream routers without direct Layer 2 connectivity.

advertise-interval.description: Interval for sending unsolicited IPv6 Router Advertisement messages in seconds. Per RFC 4861, this value must be between 180 and 1800 seconds.

ipv6-transition-mode.description:
Enable IPv6 transition-mode.
Supported modes: NAT64.

x-enumDescriptions.NAT64: Network Address Translation from IPv6 to IPv4 (NAT64) as defined in RFC 6146. Enables IPv6-only clients to access IPv4-only services through stateful address translation.

ipv6-transition-mode.x-typeDescription: IPv6 transition mechanism for facilitating communication between IPv6 and IPv4 networks. NAT64 is currently the only supported mode.

lcd.description:
Controls visibility of maintenance operations in the physical LCD menu panel on the front of the gateway.
Available only on Gateway models with LCD displays: 7010, 7030, 7024, 7205, 7210, 7220, 7240, 7240XM, 7280, 9240.
Restricting menu options prevents unauthorized physical access to factory reset, system halt, and image upgrade functions.

main-factory-default.description:
Controls visibility of the factory-default option in the LCD maintenance menu. When enabled (true), the option is visible and accessible.
When disabled (false), factory reset cannot be initiated from the physical LCD panel, providing protection against accidental or unauthorized device resets.

main-upgrade-image-part.description: Disable image upgrade partition via LCD.

menu.description:
Master enable/disable for all LCD menu functionality. When disabled, the LCD screen becomes read-only and displays only system status information.
All sub-menu controls (maintenance, factory-default, etc.) are automatically disabled.

upgrade-image-partition0.description: Disable image upgrade partition via LCD.

upgrade-image-partition1.description: Disable image upgrade partition via LCD.

location.description: Free-form text describing the physical location of the device. This value is exposed via SNMP sysLocation OID (1.3.6.1.2.1.1.6). Maximum length is platform-dependent.

logging.description: Controls local log message verbosity by module type, process, and severity level. This affects what diagnostic information is captured in the device's internal log buffers and forwarded to external syslog servers.

loopback-interface.description: References an existing Loopback Interface profile by ID. Used in conjunction with ipv4-configuration and ipv6-configuration to specify the system controller-ip address source.

radius.description: Configures the gateway's behavior as a RADIUS client including the NAS-IP-Address sent in RADIUS packets, the source interface for RADIUS communication, and the UDP port for receiving RFC 3576 (Dynamic Authorization) messages from RADIUS servers.

nas-ip.description: Radius client NAS IP address. This field can be configured only if nas-vlan is not configured.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

nas-vlan.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IP address configured on this VLAN will be used as the RADIUS client NAS-IP-Address attribute. Mutually exclusive with nas-ip.
nas-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

port.description: This field configures UDP port to receive RFC 3576 server requests.

src-interface-loopback.description:
IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in Radius packets.
This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-vlan is not configured.

src-interface-vlan.description:
Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in Radius packets.
This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-loopback is not configured.
src-interface-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

tacacs.description: Configures the gateway's behavior as a TACACS+ client, specifically controlling the source interface used for TACACS+ authentication and authorization requests to TACACS+ servers.

src-interface-loopback.description:
IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets.
This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-vlan is not configured.

src-interface-vlan.description:
Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets.
This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-loopback is not configured.
src-interface-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

timezone.description: Configures the device's timezone offset from UTC for accurate timestamp representation in logs, SNMP traps, and the LCD display. The combined hour and minute offsets determine the local time zone.

tunnel-loop-prevention.description: Prevents Layer 2 forwarding loops that can occur when traffic is encapsulated between multiple tunnels terminating on the same gateway. When enabled, the gateway tracks tunnel packet origins and drops packets that would create circular forwarding paths between GRE, IPsec, or L2TPv3 tunnels.

vpn-session-acl.description: Security policy applied to VPNC Overlay traffic.

profile.firewall.deny-inter-user-bridgin.description: Configure IPv4/IPv6 addresses to be exempted when deny-inter-user-bridging is enabled. Total IPv4 and IPv6 allowed addresses can't exceed 256

ip-address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address that needs to be allowed

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted decimal notation.
Excludes invalid/reserved addresses:
- 0.0.0.0 (unspecified address)
- 127.0.0.0/8 (loopback addresses)
- 224.0.0.0/4 (multicast addresses, 224-239.x.x.x)
- 255.255.255.255 (limited broadcast address)

An IPv6 address represented in standard notation (full, compressed, or mixed formats).
Does not include zone identifiers (e.g., %interface).
Excludes invalid/reserved addresses:
- :: (unspecified address, all zeros)
- ::1 (loopback address)
- ff00::/8 (multicast addresses, ffxx:...)

mac-address.description: mac-address that needs to be allowed

always-on-poe.description:
Always-on PoE provides ability to continue power delivery during
a soft/warm reboot. On standalone devices this applies globally,
on VSF it applies to the 'Member' and in chassis devices this is
applicable to the 'Line Cards'.

Some switch models have a restriction that all transceivers installed in
a group of ports must have compatible speeds. All mismatched interfaces
in the group will be disabled.

speed.description: Interface group speed. Device dependent, the possible speeds are 10g, 25g, 40g, 50g, 100g or 200g.

member-or-slot-ids.description:
Specifies the list of member or slot IDs to which this profile applies.
- For standalone switches: This list is ignored.
- For VSF stacks: List the member IDs that should use this profile.
- For chassis systems: List the slot IDs that should use this profile.
Note: For slot names like '1/3', only the slot number (e.g., 3) is used as the slot ID.

quick-poe.description:

in chassis devices this is applicable to the 'Line Cards'.

address.description: HTTP Proxy server's IP address or domain name.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

all-repeat-check.description: Enables all possible repeat checks avialable.

Provides ability to reduce the number of login attempts that can be made in a short time. Automatically clears the lockout after configured 'lock-out' minutes. A value of 0 indicates that lockout of users is disabled.

lowercase-count.description:
Minimum number of lowercase count in a password.
For a Gateway device, the range of values is  0-10 minimum lower case characters. A value of 0 indicates that the minimum number of lower case required is disabled by default.
For a CX device, the default value is 1 character.
For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier.
For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 lowercase characters, with a default of 2.

For a CX device, the default value is 8 characters.
For a CX device, the range is 1..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier, 1..64 otherwise.
For PVOS device, valid values range from 8 to 64.

For a Gateway device, the default value is 6 characters and the range of values is 6-128 characters.
For a CX device, the default minimum length of the password is 8 characters.
For a CX device, the range is 1..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier, 1..64 otherwise.
For PVOS device, valid values range from 0 to 64.

numeric-count.description:
Minimum number of numeric count in a password.
For a Gateway device, the range of values is 0-10 numeric digits and the default value is 0.
For a CX device, the default value is 1 character.
For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier.
For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 numeric digits, with a default of 2.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

description.description:
The RMON alarm table periodically takes statistical samples from the
SNMP MIB objects in the probe and compares them to previously
configured thresholds. A hysteresis mechanism is implemented to limit
the generation of alarm. This mechanism generates one event as a
threshold is crossed in the appropriate direction for the SNMP MIB
object. No more events are generated for that threshold until the
opposite threshold is reached.

rmon.description: RMON alarm parameters for given index.

falling-threshold.description:
Falling threshold to be compared against the current value
to trigger the SNMP alarm.

index.description: An index that uniquely identifies the RMON alarm.

interval.description:
The interval in seconds, over which the snmp-oid is sampled
and compared with the rising and falling thresholds.

rising-threshold.description:
Rising threshold to be compared against the current value
to trigger the SNMP alarm.

sample-type.description: The method of sampling of the variable.

x-enumDescriptions.ABSOLUTE:
Absolute value of the variable will be compared with the
thresholds.
x-enumDescriptions.DELTA:
The difference between the current and previous sample of
the variable will be compared with the thresholds.

sample-type.x-typeDescription: The method of sampling of the variable.

snmp-oid.description:
The object identifier to be monitored.
Only variables that resolve to an ASN.1 primitive type of INTEGER
(INTEGER, Integer32,Counter32, Counter64, Gauge32, or TimeTicks)
will be monitored.

dynamic-arp-inspection.description:
Configuration of Dynamic ARP Inspection.
Dynamic ARP Inspection is defense mechanism can be put in place on a switch to protect
against various possible attacks using ARP. This can limit the amount of ARP activity
allowed from a host or on a port and can also ensure all ARP packets are consistent
with one or more binding database which can be created via various means.
It can also enforce integrity checks on the ARP packets to check against using
different MAC or IP in the Ethernet or IP header and the ARP header.

An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

end-date-time.x-typeDescription:
A date and time, expressed in the format described in RFC3339.
That is to say:

YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ+-hh:mm

where YYYY is the year, MM is the month expressed as a two-digit
month (zero padding if required), DD is the day of the month,
expressed as a two digit value. T is the literal character 'T',
HH is the hour of the day expressed as a two digit number, using
the 24-hour clock, MM is the minute of the hour expressed as a
two digit number. Z is the literal character 'Z', followed by a
timezone offset expressed in hours (hh) and minutes (mm), both
expressed as two digit numbers. The time offset is specified as
a positive or negative offset to UTC using the '+' or '-'
character preceding the offset.

Optionally, fractional seconds can be expressed after the minute
of the hour as a decimal number of unspecified precision
reflecting fractions of a second.

Each list contains a sequence of entries with permit or deny actions and regular expression patterns to match Autonomous System paths in BGP route advertisements. AS Path Lists are used in route-maps to control route acceptance, rejection, or modification based on the path characteristics, enabling sophisticated BGP routing policies and AS-based traffic engineering

min-echo-rx-interval.description:
Sets or resets the minimum BFD echo packet reception interval.
The value 0 means that the host is not interested in receiving BFD echo packets.
The value itself is a request to the remote system that it might not be able to
honor (ex. we ask for echo packets faster than it can send them). In this scenario,
the remote system is expected to use its fastest/slowest setting (depending on
what we asked) and the session might flap.
